title: Discretionary Trust with Corporate Trustee
text:
We will establish a discretionary (family) trust with a corporate trustee to hold and manage assets on behalf of the beneficiaries.

This includes:

(a) Drafting the trust deed, setting out the rights and entitlements of the beneficiaries, the powers and obligations of the trustee, and the rules governing the operation of the trust;

(b) Establishing a new company to act as trustee of the trust, including registration with ASIC and the preparation of all required corporate documents such as the constitution, consents to act, and share certificates; 

(c) lodging the trust deed for stamping with Revenue NSW; and

(d) Providing all executed documents and registers for your records.

This fee includes one round of amendments to the trust deed.

title: Deed of Variation - Family Trust to Fixed Unit Trust
text:
Deed of Variation - Family Trust to Fixed Unit Trust (Fixed)

We will prepare a Deed of Variation to amend the existing family trust deed, converting it from a discretionary family trust to a fixed unit trust.
The deed will address the following key matters:

(a) Replacement of the discretionary distribution provisions with fixed unit entitlements, including the allocation and issuance of units to the nominated unitholders.

(b) Amendment of the trustee's powers to reflect the rights and obligations appropriate to a fixed unit trust structure.

(c) Insertion of provisions governing the transfer, redemption, and valuation of units.

(d) Ensuring the variation is consistent with the terms of the existing trust deed (including any power of variation) and does not trigger an unintended resettlement of the trust for tax purposes.

title: RAP Paper (Fixed Fee)
text:
Reasonably Arguable Position (RAP) Paper (Fixed Fee)

We will prepare a RAP paper specifically addressing whether your gambling winnings would be considered taxable income in the format of a joint venture. 

We will consider one scenario only proposed by you to inform the RAP. This allows us to keep the cost to a fixed fee. 

A position is 'reasonably arguable' if it could be concluded in the circumstances, having regard to relevant authorities, that what is argued for is about as likely to be correct as incorrect, or is more likely to be correct than incorrect. This is a higher standard than usual tax advice as it requires us to assess the issue from all potential positions before concluding on which position is "reasonably arguable".

Having a reasonably arguable position will usually protect you from administrative penalties which can be up to 90% of any tax shortfall.

The deliverable will be a detailed letter of advice setting out the Reasonably Arguable Position.

title: Fraud and Evasion Tax Return Review Advice
text:
**Tax Advice on Previous Tax Returns (estimate)**

We understand that some crypto gains/losses were not reported in your previous tax return. This is a significant amount and requires advice before any amendments are undertaken.

We will provide detailed written tax advice regarding the tax returns previously lodged, including:

**Fraud of Evasion Risk** – We will review the tax positions taken in previously lodged returns to identify the risk of a fraud or evasion finding for crypto gains/losses that were not reported.

**Amendment Requirements** – Assessing whether any amendments are legally required under Australian tax law, including any statutory obligations to correct errors or omissions.

**Period of Review** – Confirming the applicable period of review for the relevant tax years, including any extensions due to specific circumstances.

**Recommendation** - We will give a recommendation of whether any amendments should be done for previous year tax returns based on your knowledge and actions at the time, and if not how a voluntary disclosure may be done in the event of an audit or review by the ATO for returns inside the period of review.

The fee is significant here as we are required to review in detail each return lodged and the correspondence/circumstances.
